text: First workday after the holidays. The Boss cheerfully: “Rested? Great, January’s plan was due yesterday.”
left: Ask for a day to warm up

text: A colleague whispers: “I forgot my computer password. And email. And, I think, my own name.”
Accounting wants December expense reports. The receipts are somewhere among the tangerines.
Three boxes of leftover party chocolates in the kitchen. The office manager asks if she should toss them.
right: Toss them — new year, new me

text: HR launches a “New year — new goals” challenge: a 30-item survey about your dreams.
The alarm rings at 7:00, but your body is sure it’s January 1st, 3 a.m.
The department discusses who gained how much over the holidays. Eyes slowly turn to you.
right: Change the topic to the report

text: The Boss wants a “strategy for the year” by tonight. All you can think of is potato salad.
The client is back from vacation and sent 47 emails in a row marked “urgent, from last year”.
right: Call and sort it all at once

text: On the call it turns out everyone’s still in pajamas — except you. You’re the only one in a shirt.
left: Admit you’re in pajama pants too

text: Seven weeks till year-end. The Boss: “Let’s finish everything we didn’t get to this year. Starting today.”
Accounting warns: all invoices by December 15. After that it’s “year-end close, nothing accepted”.
November. You last saw the sun in October. Same with motivation.
HR sends the annual review form: “Rate yourself on 18 competencies from 1 to 10”.
The department started planning the holiday party. Theme: “Hollywood”. You need a costume.
Black Friday: everyone is on sale sites. The office Wi‑Fi is barely breathing.
The client wants a six-month project done “before New Year”.
left: Take it on and make it
right: Split it into stages till spring

text: First snow. Half the office is photographing the window, the other half is stuck in traffic.
The Boss wants “the year in numbers” by Friday. The numbers aren’t great.
right: Show them as is, with a plan

text: A colleague already hung lights on their monitor. It’s November.
right: Ask them to take it down

text: The office manager asks for help decorating the tree. There’s one string of lights, and untangling it takes half a day.
Secret Santa: you drew a coworker you’ve never talked to.
At the holiday party the host calls you on stage for a balloon contest.
The Boss scans the room: “Someone has to be on call January 2nd.” His eyes stop on you.
Accounting is closing the year and wants all invoices by tonight. Half are in your inbox, half in your memory.
After the party, photos appear in the group chat. In one of them, you’re hugging the tree.
A box of tangerines arrived. An hour later there are only peels and holiday smell left.
HR wants a holiday video greeting from your department. The script is on you.
Dec 31, 4 PM. The client: “Don’t leave! One tiny 5-minute fix”.
right: Wish happy holidays and close the laptop

text: The department decides who plays Santa at the kids’ party. The costume is already on your chair.
